statements.text: The rapid development of AI (artificial intelligence) has created growing concerns about how this technology will affect our society in the future. With this, Congress is constantly being challenged with adapting to the ever-changing global technological landscape. While legislators must address the numerous concerns and place common-sense regulations on AI technologies, it is also our duty to enact legislation that encourages innovation and ensures that the United States remains a global technology leader.
statements.venue: Official House website, issues page (Science, Space, and Technology)

statements.text: I appreciate Ranking Member McHenry for trusting me with this position. As the lead Republican on the task force, I hope to use my background in technology and information security to promote policies that encourage the integration of technology into the financial services industry and give consumers greater access to financial services. The exciting field of artificial intelligence has altered the economic landscape in America; and, in my role of leadership on this task force, I will be working to ensure that federal laws and regulations foster innovation, not stifle it.
statements.venue: Press release on appointment as lead Republican on House Financial Services AI Task Force

statements.text: I believe the execution model deserves the most attention from policymakers because it can remove the human element in decision-making.
statements.venue: House Financial Services AI Task Force hearing on AI bias and explainability (opening statement)

statements.text: I would submit that there is inherent bias in human opinion and decisions, and you can eliminate that through the machine if you have the proper data. [...] can you describe how the existing bank regulatory structure already accounts for model risks associated with AI?
statements.context: Question posed during a congressional hearing on the use of AI in regulatory technology for the financial sector.

statements.text: However, I believe that if used properly, artificial intelligence and machine learning can actually be used to reduce unfair bias.
statements.context: House hearing titled 'Keeping up with the Codes: Using AI for Effective Regtech,' where the member questions a witness about AI model risk.

statements.text: You know, artificial intelligence is a topic that spans every jurisdiction of every Committee that we have, and it is something that we need to get in front of, not behind.
statements.venue: House Administration Committee hearing on AI innovations within the Legislative Branch

statements.text: over the course of 2023, I understand there were many competing AI frameworks that agencies could have followed. Here in the House, we have a very complicated ecosystem, and we are in a situation where everyone is better off when we all row in the same direction [...] What framework did the CAO decide to use?
statements.context: House hearing on AI innovations within the legislative branch.

statements.text: Coming from an IT background, one thing about AI is, its output is only as good as the data that is used in the input. Is there any consideration of clarifying or making sure that everything that we use it for is coming from a good data set?
statements.context: House hearing on AI innovations within the legislative branch.

statements.text: I agree with some of the testimony is, if we can stop government from stamping out innovation and working to allow, with constraints, with guardrails, to protect individuals from AI.
statements.context: Opening remarks and question at a congressional hearing on AI applications in financial services and housing.

statements.text: Today, @POTUS signed the TAKE IT DOWN Act into law. As AI advances, so do the risks involved with it. This legislation will help children and their families to remove explicit or defamatory images posted online. In the digital age, privacy and security are vital and this is a major step.

I think it is really important with suspicious activity reports (SARs) especially because what I hear from a lot of financial institutions is we just do not want to get dinged by the Federal Government, right? [...] Can you talk about how Google Cloud's Anti-Money Laundering (AML) AI system uses explainable risk scores and ensures they are auditable for regulators?
statements.context: A House member questions an industry witness about AI-enabled anti-money-laundering tools at a financial services innovation hearing.

statements.text: So with that in mind, what we have seen from history is government can seriously stifle innovation if it is overly regulated. So, it is kind of a balance that we strike because we do have a need to put guardrails up but to leave this sandbox available for innovation. I think that is where we need to be looking, especially when it comes to tools like AI. There are benefits to that, and there is also reason to be fearful of the misuse of AI.
statements.context: House Financial Services Committee hearing on AI innovation in financial services, December 10, 2025.
